bench.what: The tests on the bench for a Wempe made to the model, each with how and what it must read; checks bench_wempe.json is up to date.
bench.out:
The mainspring's torque (05 06_20, 05 07 03-2; before it goes into the barrel, and again in its barrel)
    how: In its barrel, the arbor held by a lever (a 3D-printed arm 50 mm long and a hanging weight do: 1 kg at 50 mm is 0.49 N·m) or a torque gauge: wind it from slack and read the torque each half turn, then unwind and read again (the spring's friction is the difference). Leave it wound a week and read again. Once, wind it on until its coils lie tight on the arbor and count the turns from slack.
    pass: Set up ¾ turn past slack (05 06_20's "3/4 Umgang gespannt") and wound the drawn fusee's 5.08 barrel turns, the model's spring runs 424 to 839 mN·m at the level 05 06_20 measures (the solved shape, wempe_physics.js); every reading within ×0.933-1.193 of it keeps the swing in the guard band over the wind and the strip under a mainspring's stress limit (wempe_tolerances.js). From slack to coil-bound it must have the set-up, the fusee's 5.08 turns and half a turn to spare (the model's 0.96 past full wind). Unwinding reads less than winding: the coils' friction gives 1-3 % on the solved spring, mainsprings 10-20 % (ICMFF9); over 22 %, clean and grease it. After the week, still in the band.

  The pull on the fusee arbor, against 05 06_20 (05 06_20; the chain on, the barrel set up ¾ turn, before the train goes in)
    how: As Herb. Müller did in 1941 (05 06_20: "Hebellänge 262 m/m", the mean of two runs): a lever 262 mm long on the fusee arbor, and the weight (g) that holds it level read at each half turn running down from full wind (8.75 turns of the fusee, the curve's 0.05 to 8.74), twice; or a torque gauge (1 g on 262 mm is 2.57 mN·m).
    pass: Each reading within ×0.933-1.193 of the sheet's at the same turn (its readings' mean 132.7 g: 123.9-158.3 g; fully wound 138.4 g), and the run's shape the sheet's: its readings -4.7 to +4.3 % about their mean, the hump at turns 1-1.5, the dip at 4-5.75 and the rise to full wind (the solved spring through the drawn fusee fits it to 2.25 % rms). Low everywhere: the strip is thin (set up a tooth more, or a stronger strip: wempe_tolerances.js); out of shape at one end: the spring's length or set against the fusee. The sources' band, 225-270°, would want 228.6 g mean (×1.722): open (README, Unresolved).

  The train's depths (05 09 01, 05 08 02-1 (the hole tables); the plates bored and reamed, before the bushes and jewels go in)
    how: Gauge pins in each pair of holes and a micrometer, or a measuring machine, on both plates; then each mesh tried in turn with the arbors in, the escape wheel held: feel the shake at the pinion and watch the teeth through a loupe.
    pass: Centres 22.650, 18.120, 12.630, 11.850 mm (fusee-centre, centre-intermediate, intermediate-seconds, seconds-escape: the hole tables' coordinates), each within ±25 µm (gearing.js --model wempe: the seconds mesh's window less its pivots' shake; the tables give the places to 0.001 and no tolerance). A hole that errs should err wide: each mesh takes far more wide than close (-240/+436, -136/+355, -112/+281, -100/+263 µm). Closer than its window less the pivots' shake (220, 101, 62, 50 µm close): re-bush the hole, bored on the drawn centre.

  Endshake (the sheets' fits (below); each arbor in its bearings, the plates pinned and screwed, before the escapement goes in)
    how: Lift each arbor by its wheel with tweezers and watch its shoulder against a dial indicator, or feel it; the fusee arbor before its face a is re-turned (05 06 00-2: "bei Schneckenmontage ... Fläche a nachdrehen").
    pass: At 20 °C, as the Soviet Navy's 1958 MX repair book sets them (Appendix 4; the Wempe's sheets give none; the TU's 4 °C takes 3 µm of it): the centre arbor 0.07-0.10 mm (drawn 0.08, the sheets' tolerances -0.05 to 0.16), the intermediate arbor 0.07-0.10 mm (drawn 0.06, the sheets' tolerances -0.12 to 0.18), the seconds arbor 0.07-0.10 mm (drawn 0.05, the sheets' tolerances -0.14 to 0.18), the escape arbor 0.05-0.07 mm (drawn 0.06, the sheets' tolerances 0.02 to 0.08), the fusee arbor 0.08-0.12 mm (drawn 0.05, the sheets' tolerances -0.12 to 0.11), the barrel arbor 0.07-0.10 mm (drawn 0.06, the sheets' tolerances -0.13 to 0.15); the balance staff 0.04-0.06 at its endstones. The drawings' stacks come out at or just under the book's floors, so expect to free most arbors a little. The pillars' seats (0.3 +0.03 in each plate) take up to 0.06 from every arbor at once: a tight one, check the seats first. Out of the band: set the bush or jewel again, re-turn face a (the fusee), stone the shoulder.

  The balance and its hairspring vibrated (05 03_6, 05 03_7, 05 03 01-1; the spring pinned to its collet and stud, its curves bent to 05 03_7, before it goes in)
    how: Vibrate the balance on its spring in a vibrating tool (or the cock on a holder) against a master or a phone's timer: count the oscillations over two minutes, the weights against their screws' heads as drawn.
    pass: 2 oscillations a second (7,200 an hour), or slow by up to 367 s a day: the timing weights stand against their screws' heads as drawn and can only be screwed in, 5.0 turns of 73.4 s a day each (wempe_tolerances.js; their size estimated). The drawn spring on the weighed balance (2,501 g·mm²) is 7 min a day fast (0.4977 s): the strip wants 0.2841 mm, not 0.285 (0.2823-0.2869 over the steel's 200-210 GPa). No section tolerance holds the period (a µm of the strip is 455 s a day, the coil's ±0.05 ±173): fast, grind the strip thinner or choose a weaker spring; slow past the weights' reach, a stronger one.

  The balance runs down free (05 03, 05 04; the balance, hairspring and detent in, the train held still at a lock; before the mainspring is chosen)
    how: Give the balance a full swing (a twist of the movement) and let it run down, the train held. Film it from above at 30 frames a second, a card marked every 30° under it, and read the swing every few seconds (python wempe_swing.py reads a video so); time how long it takes to halve from about 207°.
    pass: The model's balance halves its swing in 35 s (its TF 111 s, set from an earlier fit of a running 6MX on video, moMvyx8eXfo, which now gives TF 105-129 s at it: wempe_startup.js). Halving in 30, 34, 35, 37, 41, 45 s (TF 80, 100, 111, 125, 160, 200): 05 06_20's drive swings it 140, 154, 161, 169, 185, 201° at 12 h; the guard's 147° at the wind's lowest wants ×1.117, 0.986, 0.933, 0.881, 0.788, 0.720 of it, the sources' 225° ×2.155, 1.845, 1.722, 1.597, 1.380, 1.224 (the strip as the drive's cube root). Shorter than 30 s, look for a pivot, the endstone or the detent's springs dragging.

  The detent rings (1436, 05 04 01-2; the detent made with its gold spring on, before it goes in)
    how: Clamp its foot as the block holds it (a printed jig with the foot's screw and two steady pins), the stone and the horn free, and flick the blade's end lightly with a hair. Record the ring with a phone a few millimetres off and read its lowest strong pitch with a spectrum app, or python benchcheck.py --ring FILE.
    pass: 98 Hz with the spring as drawn (1436's 0.09 at its ends and "0,07" at its middle, as stiff as 0.0792 mm throughout); 69-137 Hz for a spring 0.063-0.100 mm thick, half to twice the drawn stiffness, over which the detent is home before the next tooth (dynamics.js --model wempe). The pitch goes nearly as the thickness to the 1.5 (0.050 mm 49 Hz, 0.060 mm 65 Hz, 0.063 mm 69 Hz, 0.070 mm 81 Hz, 0.079 mm 98 Hz, 0.090 mm 118 Hz, 0.100 mm 137 Hz, 0.110 mm 158 Hz: wempe_tripping.js's frame clamped at the foot), so it measures the spring's section, which no figure on 1436 settles (its "0,09" would ring 118 Hz). The gold spring rings near 698 Hz: the detent's own is the lower.

  The escapement's figures and the banking (05 04_1, 05 04 01-4; the detent, its gold spring and the balance in; the train's power let down)
    how: Turn the balance slowly by hand with a protractor card under it and read each angle through a loupe; the depth of lock and the roller's shake with feeler gauges or under a measuring microscope. The preload: wire riders of known weight hung on the stone's pipe, the detent on its banking (as the Hamilton manual's Op. 78 hangs its 0.770 g).
    pass: 05 04_1's layout and the model: the impulse stone's face 28°10' before the line of centres at rest, the locking stone 37.0° on in the wheel's turn and 7.14 from its centre; the gold spring met at -1.6° of the balance, the wheel released at 11.3° with the impulse stone 5.0° inside the teeth's path (05 04_1's 5°; lock 13.0°), the gold spring off the stone at 12.8° (let-off 1.5°), the return swing past it at -11.1° (overall 23.9°); roller shake 0.011 mm, the teeth 0.39 mm into the roller. Set the banking (the block's cross screw, the 1954 instruction's п. 11) for a lock 0.237 mm deep at the stone, the middle of its window (the drawing's 0.235 lies 105 µm over its floor): never shallower than 0.130 (shallower, the stone's ring, 127 µm whatever the depth, lets a tooth past: wempe_tripping.js) nor deeper than 0.237 (the discharge stone can't lift the stone further: it doesn't unlock). A wheel at the top of its 14 +0.03 locks 0.250 deep where the drawn wheel locks 0.235: set the banking to the wheel as made. The preload at the stone: a 0.64 g rider must leave the detent on its banking and a 0.80 g one part it; aim near 0.68 g (the model's 0.8 g is an estimate: wempe_tripping.js finds a held tooth's stone ringing 44 % of the depth of lock there, under half from 0.40 g, teeth getting past at a fifth of it and under; and a 3 ms blow of 20 g across the plate lets a tooth go under 0.64 g, the floor taken here, the higher; each gram more costs about 12.8° of swing; never over 0.80 g: above it the stone, falling back after the release, lands again on the escaping tooth's back during the impulse, where the models part: dynamics.js with brass's restitution). The return pass: turn the balance back slowly by hand through the discharge with the train's power on and watch the locking stone under a loupe: the discharge stone must bend the gold spring aside without lifting the detent (wempe_tripping.js: as the model takes the stone's contact on the gold spring no tooth gets past over 333 gold's whole range of modulus, 83-110 GPa, but at 4 times that contact's stiffness 6 in 12 do, whatever the alloy: only the made spring can show it); its tip at rest 0.10-0.15 short of the discharge stone and 0.35-0.40 past the detent's end (the 1958 Navy repair book's checks, p. 60).

  The swing (—; the movement running, fully wound, at 24 h and near run-down)
    how: Read the balance's swing against marks under it, from a phone's slow-motion video (python wempe_swing.py reads the arm's sweep), or from a recording of the beat (python acoustic.py --model wempe FILE fits its clicks to the escapement in time).
    pass: In the guard band, 147-270° each way, over the whole wind (the model 155.1-165.8°, 160.7° at 12 h). The sources' band, 225-270° (the 1954 instruction, chronometers in general; the Hamilton manual 247.5-270°), is reported, not required: the model's swing is under it on 05 06_20's drive (open, README). Low at both ends with the train free: the strip doesn't suit the balance's damping (the run-down test chooses it), or the preload is high; low at one end only: the fusee's test.

  The maintaining spring drives the train (05 06 01-1, 05 06_4 (A-B); the movement running, part wound)
    how: First, assembling: the spring's eye pin up into the ratchet (05 06_4 A-B: "Stift nach oben"), its other pin down into the fusee wheel; the ring lies free in the wheel's recess, its eye a gap short of its square end. Running, the ratchet stands ahead of the wheel as the drive closes the ring: see its ends nearly meet, not touch. Then turn the key back a little (winding) and hold it still, the fusee off the train: time how long the balance keeps going.
    pass: Running, the ring closed 14.4-15.6° by the drive, its ends 0.27-0.58 mm apart at the eye (they would meet after 16.7°; wempe_sustaining.js); the key held, the balance keeps going 7.7-10.9 minutes (the detent catching a whole tooth late or at once), its swing falling; the 1954 instruction gives 1-2 minutes for chronometers in general; a wind takes 10-30 s. Under 5 minutes (estimated): the ring is open (the pins the wrong way round: it bears on the recess's wall and barely gives), weak, or has taken a set; its ends touching in running: weak or set.

  The stop work: the bar springs back, the stop holds full wind (05 06_4 (C-D), 05 06 04-2, 05 08 (hole 7); the bar, its spring and pin in the fusee's small end, the cover plate off; then the fusee in its plates, the chain on and the barrel set up, the train out)
    how: Cover plate off: push the bar in from its lower end with a pegwood to its full 3.6 and let go, the small end up and then down; repeat ten times. Then, assembled, wind slowly to the stop and count the fusee's turns from run-down; let the chain run back a quarter turn and wind again.
    pass: The bar springs fully out at once every time, in both positions: its spring (05 06 03-3; no source draws its section: any height 0.9-1.5, its pin's hole to the recess's floor, 0.10 thick; wempe_strength.js) pushes it 0.06-0.08 N half way at the model's 1.0 high, 41 times or more the 0.5 g bar's sliding on the cover plate (μ 0.3, estimated). Assembled: the stop pin (hole 7) stops the fusee with the chain 8.638 turns on it (8.70 from run-down), 0.112 turn short of the groove's end N, and the bar never touches the pin earlier (0.69 off a turn before: wempe_stopwork.py). Sluggish: clean the slot and the bar, and look for a burr at the slot's ends; still slow, bend the spring's free span further in, keeping it under its steel's yield (wempe_strength.js). Stopping short of 8.64 turns: the bar is caught early (its spring too weak to hold it out, or the bar's upper end too long).

  The stop takes a strong hand, and the key is one-way (05 08 01-5, 05 06_4 (C-D), 51 00 11; the stop bar and pin hardened, the movement wound to the stop; the key made)
    how: File-test the stop bar and the stop pin (a file skates on hardened steel). Wound to full wind, hold the key against the stop with a torque gauge on its square (or a lever and a weight) up to 1.36 N·m, a strong hand's on the key's Ø 34.5 paddle (wempe_overwind.js). Then turn the key the wrong way on a spare square held in a vice with a gauge: it must slip.
    pass: Nothing moves or marks: hardened, the stop bar yields at 3.63 N·m on the key and the pin at 9.87; left soft the bar bends at 1.31. The key's coil spring carries the hand: wound of spring wire Ø 0.68 or more (EN 10270-1 DH; 51 00 11 scales about 0.6, which yields at 1.57), its end in the body's hole formed on a radius. The wrong way it slips at a few mN·m (the model takes 5): one that grips both ways sends the hand into the click wheel, whose teeth yield at 0.72 N·m (the 1940 key is one-way too: its click spring, 05-01_6).

  The cannon pinion's friction (05 05 03-3, 05 02 00-1; the motion work and the hands on, the movement level)
    how: Hang a weight on the minute hand 30 mm from its arbor, the hand horizontal, and see whether it turns the hand (the cannon pinion slipping on the centre arbor).
    pass: It slips between 10.3 and 446 g (wempe_motionwork.js, wempe_transmission.js's window: looser, a 45 g knock turns the hands; tighter, setting them forward drives the balance to the escapement's trip): set it near 68 g. Set the hands forward only (the 6MX's instruction: backward "can break the escape wheel's teeth"): a fit near the window's top would turn the train back against its locking stone near run-down.

  The rate, and the 6MX TU's trial (6MX TU 25-07-1533-84 (6MX-figures.md); cased, in its gimbals, rated)
    how: Each day at the same hour compare it with a time signal to a tenth of a second and log the error (python rating.py works the daily rates). The trial: 35 days in five periods of seven at 36, 20, 4, 20, 36 °C (a wine cooler, a room, a box with a lamp and a thermostat), the first two days of each not counted, wound daily after the comparison to "8" on the up-and-down dial, to "0" at each period's end.
    pass: The TU's figures (losing positive): E, the mean of |each counted rate − its period's mean|, within ±0.35; R = ω_V − ω_I ±2.00; D, the largest change between consecutive rates in a period, ±2.30; C = (ω36 − ω4)/32 ±0.10 s a day a °C; S = (ω36 + ω4)/2 − ω20 ±1.20; every period's mean ±3.50; N = 42E + 4.5R + 60C + 2.4S ≤ 30 (wempe_errorbudget.js passes it as adjusted). Out on C: move the four masses along the rim ("8 Körner in 60 Teilung", 6° a division) by trial: at the drawn place (30° from the cuts' line) the balance loses 2.70 s a day a °C, they null it near 18.5° from the cuts' line, a degree along the rim 0.224 s a day a °C (wempe_thermal.js). For a chronometer to navigate by (about 2 miles of longitude a month: wempe_errorbudget.js's voyage, 6 s at 30 days against 17 s with the 6MX passports' ±0.45°), go on past the TU's ±0.10: repeat the 4 °C and 36 °C periods (five counted days each, which measure C to about ±0.005) and move the masses by C / 0.224 degrees each round until |C| is within ±0.022 s a day a °C, the masses within ±0.1° of their place: 27 µm along the rim at r 15.7, both of a pair moved alike to keep the poise, against a scribed line under a 10× loupe; two or three rounds. Out on S past ±1.20: the nickel steel isn't Guillaume's integral alloy (wempe_thermal.js).

  ok  tools/bench_wempe.json is up to date
  (355 s)

tolerances.what: How closely the parts the drawings don’t size must be made: each range keeping the swing in the guard band over the whole wind; checks tolerances_wempe.json is up to date.
tolerances.out:
The swing's band over the wind
  the drive over the wind (05 06_20 through the train): 0.954 of the reference at 55.3 h to 1.043 at 0.0 h; the swing 155.1-165.8° (at 12 h 160.7°)
  the guard band 147-270° (wempe_escapement.js's: the model's own swing is under the sources'), and the sources' 225-270° (the 1954 instruction; the Hamilton manual 247.5-270°), reported

The mainspring (05 06_20: "Zugfeder 15 × 0,37", no tolerance; its length on no sheet, solved 1,240 mm)
  the swing stays in the guard band over the whole wind for a drive 0.934-2.127 of 05 06_20's (−7 % to +113 %); the strip's stress fully wound at the measured level is 2.45 GPa (wempe_physics.js), which a strip of the same set reaches at a mainspring's limit, 2.6 GPa, at 1.193 of the drive: the stress, not the swing, sets the top
    so 0.934-1.193 (−7 % to +19 %): the strip 0.362-0.392 mm at the drawn 15 mm and solved 1,240 mm, if 0.370 gives the measured pull; at the measured level the solved spring's strip is 0.370 (wempe_physics.js), so 0.362-0.393 on it
    read as 05 06_20 reads it (g on a 262 mm lever on the fusee arbor, running down): its 24 readings' mean 132.7 g (the sheet's own 131.5) within 123.9-158.3 g, fully wound 138.4 within 129.2-165.1; the escapement's rate at the 12 h reference moves −1.79 to +3.41 s a day there (the timing takes it up)
    the sources' band wants at least 1.722 of the measured drive at the wind's lowest (+72 %: the strip 0.444 mm on the drawn 0.370, 228.6 g mean on 05 06_20's lever), past the stress limit's 1.193: not by the strip alone: the drive's level is the open question (README, Unresolved)

The detent's spring (1436: "0,07", faint; its other figure "0,09") and its preload (the banking, not drawn)
  its stiffness E b t³/12 L (steel, 1.9 wide, 5 long) goes as its thickness cubed; the preload is the banking's (makeEsc's W78, 0.8 g at the stone, estimated), left as set. The swing stays above 147° at the wind's lowest drive up to 3.3 times the drawn stiffness (0.117 mm thick); with no stiffness at all it swings 164.0° at 12 h: its work sets no lower limit
    1436's other figure, 0.09 (1.47 times as stiff): 153.5-164.2° over the wind; the spring's lower limit is the detent's return in time, which dynamics.js --model wempe checks from half to twice the drawn stiffness (0.063-0.100 mm): home before the next tooth over all of it
  the preload: 0.3 g 161.6-171.9°, 0.8 g 155.1-165.8°, 1 g 152.4-163.2°, 1.5 g 146.1-157.3° over the wind; at least 0.64 g, the higher of the least that lets no tooth past in the frame, 0.40 g (wempe_tripping.js: 0×, 0.1×, 0.2× the estimate let teeth past; a held tooth's stone rings 53.9 % of the depth of lock at the estimate 0.8 g and under half only from 0.93 g, reported), and the knock's, 0.64 g (a 3 ms blow of 20 g across the plate lets no tooth go from there: 26.6 g at the estimate), at most 0.80 g, the lower of the stone's landing on the escaping tooth's back during the impulse, which it never does up to 0.80 g (dynamics.js, brass's restitution 0.80-0.95), and the swing at the wind's lowest at 147° (1.43 g)

The gold spring (05 04 01-2: 0.15 thick, sure; 333 gold, its modulus 98 GPa: Au/Ag/Cu 333-333, likely)
  it bends on the return swing as the discharge stone passes and its work is lost: the swing stays above 147° at the wind's lowest drive up to 1.29 times its stiffness (E t³: the strip 0.163 mm at 98 GPa, or the alloy's modulus 127 GPa at 0.15); with none 185.0° at 12 h; half as stiff 168.1-178.0° over the wind
    softer is free for the swing but not for the lock: wempe_tripping.js's sweep on the drawn detent (12 November 2026, the discharge stone at 05 04_1's 5°, the lock 0.235 and the preload 0.8 g) has a held tooth's stone ringing 65 % of the depth of lock with the gold spring half as stiff, against 54 % as drawn (71 % and 49 % on 19 October 2026, the stone as it was; 64 % and 44 % at 0.175 and 0.63 g; 51 % and 42 % with the straight horn): its alloy's modulus is the open part (README, Unresolved)

The depth of lock (05 04_1: the tips 0.235 into the stone's flat; the wheel Ø 14 +0.03, 05 04_23; the banking sets it)
  as drawn 0.235 mm deep: lock 13.0°, let-off 1.5°, the stone lifted 0.257 mm at the release; 155.1-160.7° (the wind's lowest, 12 h)
  deepest that unlocks with the swing in the guard band: 0.2436 mm at 20 °C, 0.2372 set at 20 °C to hold at 36 °C (wempe_thermal_frame.js: the gold spring's tip drawn back, the let-off taken; the window's top 0.2372)
  at 0.2372 mm (the discharge stone lifts the stone at most 0.269 mm); there lock 13.0°, let-off 1.5°, 155.1° at the wind's lowest
  shallowest that lets no tooth past in the frame (wempe_tripping.js: one gets past at 0.120; a held tooth's stone rings 127 µm as drawn, 53.9 % of the depth, the gold spring's blow on the return, which doesn't go with the lock): 0.130 mm; there lock 7.7°, 173.3-179.0° (a shallower lock gives the swing back: the unlocking costs less)
  the wheel's tips Ø 14 +0.03: with the banking left where the drawn wheel puts it, a wheel at the top of its tolerance locks 0.250 deep, past 0.237: it would not unlock. The banking is set to the wheel as made
  ~~ by tripping.js's rule for the Hamilton (a held tooth's stone under half the depth of lock) the drawn version has no window: twice its ring, 0.254 mm, is past the 0.2436 that unlocks, and the preload that halves it, 0.93 g, is over its cap, 0.80 g. Reported: the ring turns on one estimate, the discharge stone's stiffness on the gold spring's tip on the return (README, Unresolved)

The hairspring (05 03_6: strip 0.285 × 0.52, boxed, no tolerance; coil Ø 12.8 ±0.05, boxed; cut to 13 turns less 3.5 mm, 05 03_7) against the period
  as drawn (505.4 mm, 206 GPa) with the weighed balance (2565.5 g·mm²) the period is 0.4977 s: 7 min a day fast against the train's 0.5 s
  each µm of the strip's thickness moves the rate 455 s a day, each 0.01 mm of the coil's Ø 35 (the drawn ±0.05: ±173), each mm of its length 85, each GPa of the steel's modulus 210 (200-210: ±1049)
  a turn of both timing weights (0.730 g together at r 18.66, the screws' 0.16 pitch) moves it 73.4 s a day; as drawn they stand against their screws' heads 0.80 mm off the rim (their size estimated), so they can only be screwed in, 5.0 turns, gaining up to 367 s a day
  so the period is matched, not made: 0.5 s wants the strip 0.2841 mm at 206 GPa (0.2823-0.2869 over 200-210), and the weights' reach is 0.81 µm of it; the coil's own ±0.05 is 0.5 times their reach. A 1940s spring was vibrated against the balance and chosen or ground to it; the bench's test (wempe_bench.js) times it so

  ok  tools/tolerances_wempe.json is what this finds
  (501 s)

bench.note: tools/wempe_bench.js: the tests on the bench for a Wempe made to the model, each with how and what it must read, and their figures as numbers (criteria: wempe_montecarlo.js, the Wempe's verification report)

tests.title: The mainspring's torque
tests.when: before it goes into the barrel, and again in its barrel
tests.how: In its barrel, the arbor held by a lever (a 3D-printed arm 50 mm long and a hanging weight do: 1 kg at 50 mm is 0.49 N·m) or a torque gauge: wind it from slack and read the torque each half turn, then unwind and read again (the spring's friction is the difference). Leave it wound a week and read again. Once, wind it on until its coils lie tight on the arbor and count the turns from slack.
tests.pass: Set up ¾ turn past slack (05 06_20's "3/4 Umgang gespannt") and wound the drawn fusee's 5.08 barrel turns, the model's spring runs 424 to 839 mN·m at the level 05 06_20 measures (the solved shape, wempe_physics.js); every reading within ×0.933-1.193 of it keeps the swing in the guard band over the wind and the strip under a mainspring's stress limit (wempe_tolerances.js). From slack to coil-bound it must have the set-up, the fusee's 5.08 turns and half a turn to spare (the model's 0.96 past full wind). Unwinding reads less than winding: the coils' friction gives 1-3 % on the solved spring, mainsprings 10-20 % (ICMFF9); over 22 %, clean and grease it. After the week, still in the band.

tests.title: The pull on the fusee arbor, against 05 06_20
tests.when: the chain on, the barrel set up ¾ turn, before the train goes in
tests.how: As Herb. Müller did in 1941 (05 06_20: "Hebellänge 262 m/m", the mean of two runs): a lever 262 mm long on the fusee arbor, and the weight (g) that holds it level read at each half turn running down from full wind (8.75 turns of the fusee, the curve's 0.05 to 8.74), twice; or a torque gauge (1 g on 262 mm is 2.57 mN·m).
tests.pass: Each reading within ×0.933-1.193 of the sheet's at the same turn (its readings' mean 132.7 g: 123.9-158.3 g; fully wound 138.4 g), and the run's shape the sheet's: its readings -4.7 to +4.3 % about their mean, the hump at turns 1-1.5, the dip at 4-5.75 and the rise to full wind (the solved spring through the drawn fusee fits it to 2.25 % rms). Low everywhere: the strip is thin (set up a tooth more, or a stronger strip: wempe_tolerances.js); out of shape at one end: the spring's length or set against the fusee. The sources' band, 225-270°, would want 228.6 g mean (×1.722): open (README, Unresolved).

tests.title: The train's depths
tests.when: the plates bored and reamed, before the bushes and jewels go in
tests.how: Gauge pins in each pair of holes and a micrometer, or a measuring machine, on both plates; then each mesh tried in turn with the arbors in, the escape wheel held: feel the shake at the pinion and watch the teeth through a loupe.
tests.pass: Centres 22.650, 18.120, 12.630, 11.850 mm (fusee-centre, centre-intermediate, intermediate-seconds, seconds-escape: the hole tables' coordinates), each within ±25 µm (gearing.js --model wempe: the seconds mesh's window less its pivots' shake; the tables give the places to 0.001 and no tolerance). A hole that errs should err wide: each mesh takes far more wide than close (-240/+436, -136/+355, -112/+281, -100/+263 µm). Closer than its window less the pivots' shake (220, 101, 62, 50 µm close): re-bush the hole, bored on the drawn centre.

tests.title: Endshake
tests.when: each arbor in its bearings, the plates pinned and screwed, before the escapement goes in
tests.how: Lift each arbor by its wheel with tweezers and watch its shoulder against a dial indicator, or feel it; the fusee arbor before its face a is re-turned (05 06 00-2: "bei Schneckenmontage ... Fläche a nachdrehen").
tests.pass: At 20 °C, as the Soviet Navy's 1958 MX repair book sets them (Appendix 4; the Wempe's sheets give none; the TU's 4 °C takes 3 µm of it): the centre arbor 0.07-0.10 mm (drawn 0.08, the sheets' tolerances -0.05 to 0.16), the intermediate arbor 0.07-0.10 mm (drawn 0.06, the sheets' tolerances -0.12 to 0.18), the seconds arbor 0.07-0.10 mm (drawn 0.05, the sheets' tolerances -0.14 to 0.18), the escape arbor 0.05-0.07 mm (drawn 0.06, the sheets' tolerances 0.02 to 0.08), the fusee arbor 0.08-0.12 mm (drawn 0.05, the sheets' tolerances -0.12 to 0.11), the barrel arbor 0.07-0.10 mm (drawn 0.06, the sheets' tolerances -0.13 to 0.15); the balance staff 0.04-0.06 at its endstones. The drawings' stacks come out at or just under the book's floors, so expect to free most arbors a little. The pillars' seats (0.3 +0.03 in each plate) take up to 0.06 from every arbor at once: a tight one, check the seats first. Out of the band: set the bush or jewel again, re-turn face a (the fusee), stone the shoulder.

tests.title: The balance and its hairspring vibrated
tests.when: the spring pinned to its collet and stud, its curves bent to 05 03_7, before it goes in
tests.how: Vibrate the balance on its spring in a vibrating tool (or the cock on a holder) against a master or a phone's timer: count the oscillations over two minutes, the weights against their screws' heads as drawn.
tests.pass: 2 oscillations a second (7,200 an hour), or slow by up to 367 s a day: the timing weights stand against their screws' heads as drawn and can only be screwed in, 5.0 turns of 73.4 s a day each (wempe_tolerances.js; their size estimated). The drawn spring on the weighed balance (2,501 g·mm²) is 7 min a day fast (0.4977 s): the strip wants 0.2841 mm, not 0.285 (0.2823-0.2869 over the steel's 200-210 GPa). No section tolerance holds the period (a µm of the strip is 455 s a day, the coil's ±0.05 ±173): fast, grind the strip thinner or choose a weaker spring; slow past the weights' reach, a stronger one.

tests.title: The balance runs down free
tests.when: the balance, hairspring and detent in, the train held still at a lock; before the mainspring is chosen
tests.how: Give the balance a full swing (a twist of the movement) and let it run down, the train held. Film it from above at 30 frames a second, a card marked every 30° under it, and read the swing every few seconds (python wempe_swing.py reads a video so); time how long it takes to halve from about 207°.
tests.pass: The model's balance halves its swing in 35 s (its TF 111 s, set from an earlier fit of a running 6MX on video, moMvyx8eXfo, which now gives TF 105-129 s at it: wempe_startup.js). Halving in 30, 34, 35, 37, 41, 45 s (TF 80, 100, 111, 125, 160, 200): 05 06_20's drive swings it 140, 154, 161, 169, 185, 201° at 12 h; the guard's 147° at the wind's lowest wants ×1.117, 0.986, 0.933, 0.881, 0.788, 0.720 of it, the sources' 225° ×2.155, 1.845, 1.722, 1.597, 1.380, 1.224 (the strip as the drive's cube root). Shorter than 30 s, look for a pivot, the endstone or the detent's springs dragging.

tests.title: The detent rings
tests.when: the detent made with its gold spring on, before it goes in
tests.how: Clamp its foot as the block holds it (a printed jig with the foot's screw and two steady pins), the stone and the horn free, and flick the blade's end lightly with a hair. Record the ring with a phone a few millimetres off and read its lowest strong pitch with a spectrum app, or python benchcheck.py --ring FILE.
tests.pass: 98 Hz with the spring as drawn (1436's 0.09 at its ends and "0,07" at its middle, as stiff as 0.0792 mm throughout); 69-137 Hz for a spring 0.063-0.100 mm thick, half to twice the drawn stiffness, over which the detent is home before the next tooth (dynamics.js --model wempe). The pitch goes nearly as the thickness to the 1.5 (0.050 mm 49 Hz, 0.060 mm 65 Hz, 0.063 mm 69 Hz, 0.070 mm 81 Hz, 0.079 mm 98 Hz, 0.090 mm 118 Hz, 0.100 mm 137 Hz, 0.110 mm 158 Hz: wempe_tripping.js's frame clamped at the foot), so it measures the spring's section, which no figure on 1436 settles (its "0,09" would ring 118 Hz). The gold spring rings near 698 Hz: the detent's own is the lower.

tests.title: The escapement's figures and the banking
tests.when: the detent, its gold spring and the balance in; the train's power let down
tests.how: Turn the balance slowly by hand with a protractor card under it and read each angle through a loupe; the depth of lock and the roller's shake with feeler gauges or under a measuring microscope. The preload: wire riders of known weight hung on the stone's pipe, the detent on its banking (as the Hamilton manual's Op. 78 hangs its 0.770 g).
tests.pass: 05 04_1's layout and the model: the impulse stone's face 28°10' before the line of centres at rest, the locking stone 37.0° on in the wheel's turn and 7.14 from its centre; the gold spring met at -1.6° of the balance, the wheel released at 11.3° with the impulse stone 5.0° inside the teeth's path (05 04_1's 5°; lock 13.0°), the gold spring off the stone at 12.8° (let-off 1.5°), the return swing past it at -11.1° (overall 23.9°); roller shake 0.011 mm, the teeth 0.39 mm into the roller. Set the banking (the block's cross screw, the 1954 instruction's п. 11) for a lock 0.237 mm deep at the stone, the middle of its window (the drawing's 0.235 lies 105 µm over its floor): never shallower than 0.130 (shallower, the stone's ring, 127 µm whatever the depth, lets a tooth past: wempe_tripping.js) nor deeper than 0.237 (the discharge stone can't lift the stone further: it doesn't unlock). A wheel at the top of its 14 +0.03 locks 0.250 deep where the drawn wheel locks 0.235: set the banking to the wheel as made. The preload at the stone: a 0.64 g rider must leave the detent on its banking and a 0.80 g one part it; aim near 0.68 g (the model's 0.8 g is an estimate: wempe_tripping.js finds a held tooth's stone ringing 44 % of the depth of lock there, under half from 0.40 g, teeth getting past at a fifth of it and under; and a 3 ms blow of 20 g across the plate lets a tooth go under 0.64 g, the floor taken here, the higher; each gram more costs about 12.8° of swing; never over 0.80 g: above it the stone, falling back after the release, lands again on the escaping tooth's back during the impulse, where the models part: dynamics.js with brass's restitution). The return pass: turn the balance back slowly by hand through the discharge with the train's power on and watch the locking stone under a loupe: the discharge stone must bend the gold spring aside without lifting the detent (wempe_tripping.js: as the model takes the stone's contact on the gold spring no tooth gets past over 333 gold's whole range of modulus, 83-110 GPa, but at 4 times that contact's stiffness 6 in 12 do, whatever the alloy: only the made spring can show it); its tip at rest 0.10-0.15 short of the discharge stone and 0.35-0.40 past the detent's end (the 1958 Navy repair book's checks, p. 60).

tests.title: The swing
tests.when: the movement running, fully wound, at 24 h and near run-down
tests.how: Read the balance's swing against marks under it, from a phone's slow-motion video (python wempe_swing.py reads the arm's sweep), or from a recording of the beat (python acoustic.py --model wempe FILE fits its clicks to the escapement in time).
tests.pass: In the guard band, 147-270° each way, over the whole wind (the model 155.1-165.8°, 160.7° at 12 h). The sources' band, 225-270° (the 1954 instruction, chronometers in general; the Hamilton manual 247.5-270°), is reported, not required: the model's swing is under it on 05 06_20's drive (open, README). Low at both ends with the train free: the strip doesn't suit the balance's damping (the run-down test chooses it), or the preload is high; low at one end only: the fusee's test.

tests.title: The maintaining spring drives the train
tests.when: the movement running, part wound
tests.how: First, assembling: the spring's eye pin up into the ratchet (05 06_4 A-B: "Stift nach oben"), its other pin down into the fusee wheel; the ring lies free in the wheel's recess, its eye a gap short of its square end. Running, the ratchet stands ahead of the wheel as the drive closes the ring: see its ends nearly meet, not touch. Then turn the key back a little (winding) and hold it still, the fusee off the train: time how long the balance keeps going.
tests.pass: Running, the ring closed 14.4-15.6° by the drive, its ends 0.27-0.58 mm apart at the eye (they would meet after 16.7°; wempe_sustaining.js); the key held, the balance keeps going 7.7-10.9 minutes (the detent catching a whole tooth late or at once), its swing falling; the 1954 instruction gives 1-2 minutes for chronometers in general; a wind takes 10-30 s. Under 5 minutes (estimated): the ring is open (the pins the wrong way round: it bears on the recess's wall and barely gives), weak, or has taken a set; its ends touching in running: weak or set.

tests.title: The stop work: the bar springs back, the stop holds full wind
tests.when: the bar, its spring and pin in the fusee's small end, the cover plate off; then the fusee in its plates, the chain on and the barrel set up, the train out
tests.how: Cover plate off: push the bar in from its lower end with a pegwood to its full 3.6 and let go, the small end up and then down; repeat ten times. Then, assembled, wind slowly to the stop and count the fusee's turns from run-down; let the chain run back a quarter turn and wind again.
tests.pass: The bar springs fully out at once every time, in both positions: its spring (05 06 03-3; no source draws its section: any height 0.9-1.5, its pin's hole to the recess's floor, 0.10 thick; wempe_strength.js) pushes it 0.06-0.08 N half way at the model's 1.0 high, 41 times or more the 0.5 g bar's sliding on the cover plate (μ 0.3, estimated). Assembled: the stop pin (hole 7) stops the fusee with the chain 8.638 turns on it (8.70 from run-down), 0.112 turn short of the groove's end N, and the bar never touches the pin earlier (0.69 off a turn before: wempe_stopwork.py). Sluggish: clean the slot and the bar, and look for a burr at the slot's ends; still slow, bend the spring's free span further in, keeping it under its steel's yield (wempe_strength.js). Stopping short of 8.64 turns: the bar is caught early (its spring too weak to hold it out, or the bar's upper end too long).

tests.title: The stop takes a strong hand, and the key is one-way
tests.when: the stop bar and pin hardened, the movement wound to the stop; the key made
tests.how: File-test the stop bar and the stop pin (a file skates on hardened steel). Wound to full wind, hold the key against the stop with a torque gauge on its square (or a lever and a weight) up to 1.36 N·m, a strong hand's on the key's Ø 34.5 paddle (wempe_overwind.js). Then turn the key the wrong way on a spare square held in a vice with a gauge: it must slip.
tests.pass: Nothing moves or marks: hardened, the stop bar yields at 3.63 N·m on the key and the pin at 9.87; left soft the bar bends at 1.31. The key's coil spring carries the hand: wound of spring wire Ø 0.68 or more (EN 10270-1 DH; 51 00 11 scales about 0.6, which yields at 1.57), its end in the body's hole formed on a radius. The wrong way it slips at a few mN·m (the model takes 5): one that grips both ways sends the hand into the click wheel, whose teeth yield at 0.72 N·m (the 1940 key is one-way too: its click spring, 05-01_6).

tests.title: The cannon pinion's friction
tests.when: the motion work and the hands on, the movement level
tests.how: Hang a weight on the minute hand 30 mm from its arbor, the hand horizontal, and see whether it turns the hand (the cannon pinion slipping on the centre arbor).
tests.pass: It slips between 10.3 and 446 g (wempe_motionwork.js, wempe_transmission.js's window: looser, a 45 g knock turns the hands; tighter, setting them forward drives the balance to the escapement's trip): set it near 68 g. Set the hands forward only (the 6MX's instruction: backward "can break the escape wheel's teeth"): a fit near the window's top would turn the train back against its locking stone near run-down.

tests.title: The rate, and the 6MX TU's trial
tests.when: cased, in its gimbals, rated
tests.how: Each day at the same hour compare it with a time signal to a tenth of a second and log the error (python rating.py works the daily rates). The trial: 35 days in five periods of seven at 36, 20, 4, 20, 36 °C (a wine cooler, a room, a box with a lamp and a thermostat), the first two days of each not counted, wound daily after the comparison to "8" on the up-and-down dial, to "0" at each period's end.
tests.pass: The TU's figures (losing positive): E, the mean of |each counted rate − its period's mean|, within ±0.35; R = ω_V − ω_I ±2.00; D, the largest change between consecutive rates in a period, ±2.30; C = (ω36 − ω4)/32 ±0.10 s a day a °C; S = (ω36 + ω4)/2 − ω20 ±1.20; every period's mean ±3.50; N = 42E + 4.5R + 60C + 2.4S ≤ 30 (wempe_errorbudget.js passes it as adjusted). Out on C: move the four masses along the rim ("8 Körner in 60 Teilung", 6° a division) by trial: at the drawn place (30° from the cuts' line) the balance loses 2.70 s a day a °C, they null it near 18.5° from the cuts' line, a degree along the rim 0.224 s a day a °C (wempe_thermal.js). For a chronometer to navigate by (about 2 miles of longitude a month: wempe_errorbudget.js's voyage, 6 s at 30 days against 17 s with the 6MX passports' ±0.45°), go on past the TU's ±0.10: repeat the 4 °C and 36 °C periods (five counted days each, which measure C to about ±0.005) and move the masses by C / 0.224 degrees each round until |C| is within ±0.022 s a day a °C, the masses within ±0.1° of their place: 27 µm along the rim at r 15.7, both of a pair moved alike to keep the poise, against a scribed line under a 10× loupe; two or three rounds. Out on S past ±1.20: the nickel steel isn't Guillaume's integral alloy (wempe_thermal.js).

tests.title: The mainspring's torque
tests.when: before it goes into the barrel, and again in its barrel
tests.how: In its barrel, the arbor held by a lever (a 3D-printed arm 50 mm long and a hanging weight do: 1 kg at 50 mm is 0.49 N·m) or a torque gauge: wind it from slack and read the torque each half turn, then unwind and read again (the spring's friction is the difference). Leave it wound a week and read again. Once, wind it on until its coils lie tight on the arbor and count the turns from slack.
tests.pass: Set up ¾ turn past slack (05 06_20's "3/4 Umgang gespannt") and wound the drawn fusee's 5.08 barrel turns, the model's spring runs 424 to 839 mN·m at the level 05 06_20 measures (the solved shape, wempe_physics.js); every reading within ×0.797-1.193 of it keeps the swing in the guard band over the wind and the strip under a mainspring's stress limit (wempe_tolerances.js). From slack to coil-bound it must have the set-up, the fusee's 5.08 turns and half a turn to spare (the model's 0.96 past full wind). Unwinding reads less than winding: the coils' friction gives 1-3 % on the solved spring, mainsprings 10-20 % (ICMFF9); over 22 %, clean and grease it. After the week, still in the band.

tests.title: The pull on the fusee arbor, against 05 06_20
tests.when: the chain on, the barrel set up ¾ turn, before the train goes in
tests.how: As Herb. Müller did in 1941 (05 06_20: "Hebellänge 262 m/m", the mean of two runs): a lever 262 mm long on the fusee arbor, and the weight (g) that holds it level read at each half turn running down from full wind (8.75 turns of the fusee, the curve's 0.05 to 8.74), twice; or a torque gauge (1 g on 262 mm is 2.57 mN·m).
tests.pass: Each reading within ×0.797-1.193 of the sheet's at the same turn (its readings' mean 132.7 g: 105.8-158.3 g; fully wound 138.4 g), and the run's shape the sheet's: its readings -4.7 to +4.3 % about their mean, the hump at turns 1-1.5, the dip at 4-5.75 and the rise to full wind (the solved spring through the drawn fusee fits it to 2.25 % rms). Low everywhere: the strip is thin (set up a tooth more, or a stronger strip: wempe_tolerances.js); out of shape at one end: the spring's length or set against the fusee. The sources' band, 225-270°, would want 210.9 g mean (×1.589): open (README, Unresolved).

tests.title: The train's depths
tests.when: the plates bored and reamed, before the bushes and jewels go in
tests.how: Gauge pins in each pair of holes and a micrometer, or a measuring machine, on both plates; then each mesh tried in turn with the arbors in, the escape wheel held: feel the shake at the pinion and watch the teeth through a loupe.
tests.pass: Centres 22.650, 18.120, 12.630, 11.850 mm (fusee-centre, centre-intermediate, intermediate-seconds, seconds-escape: the hole tables' coordinates), each within ±25 µm (gearing.js --model wempe: the seconds mesh's window less its pivots' shake; the tables give the places to 0.001 and no tolerance). A hole that errs should err wide: each mesh takes far more wide than close (-240/+436, -136/+355, -112/+281, -100/+263 µm). Closer than its window less the pivots' shake (220, 101, 62, 50 µm close): re-bush the hole, bored on the drawn centre.

tests.title: Endshake
tests.when: each arbor in its bearings, the plates pinned and screwed, before the escapement goes in
tests.how: Lift each arbor by its wheel with tweezers and watch its shoulder against a dial indicator, or feel it; the fusee arbor before its face a is re-turned (05 06 00-2: "bei Schneckenmontage ... Fläche a nachdrehen").
tests.pass: At 20 °C, as the Soviet Navy's 1958 MX repair book sets them (Appendix 4; the Wempe's sheets give none; the TU's 4 °C takes 3 µm of it): the centre arbor 0.07-0.10 mm (drawn 0.08, the sheets' tolerances -0.05 to 0.16), the intermediate arbor 0.07-0.10 mm (drawn 0.06, the sheets' tolerances -0.12 to 0.18), the seconds arbor 0.07-0.10 mm (drawn 0.05, the sheets' tolerances -0.14 to 0.18), the escape arbor 0.05-0.07 mm (drawn 0.06, the sheets' tolerances 0.02 to 0.08), the fusee arbor 0.08-0.12 mm (drawn 0.05, the sheets' tolerances -0.12 to 0.11), the barrel arbor 0.07-0.10 mm (drawn 0.06, the sheets' tolerances -0.13 to 0.15); the balance staff 0.04-0.06 at its endstones. tests.title: The balance and its hairspring vibrated

Assembled: the stop pin (hole 7) stops the fusee with the chain 8.638 turns on it (8.70 from run-down), 0.112 turn short of the groove's end N, and the bar never touches the pin earlier (0.69 off a turn before: wempe_stopwork.py). Sluggish: clean the slot and the bar, and look for a burr at the slot's ends; still slow, bend the spring's free span further in, keeping it under its steel's yield (wempe_strength.js). Stopping short of 8.64 turns: the bar is caught early (its spring too weak to hold it out, or the bar's upper end too long).

tests.title: The stop takes a strong hand, and the key is one-way
tests.when: the stop bar and pin hardened, the movement wound to the stop; the key made
tests.how: File-test the stop bar and the stop pin (a file skates on hardened steel). Wound to full wind, hold the key against the stop with a torque gauge on its square (or a lever and a weight) up to 1.36 N·m, a strong hand's on the key's Ø 34.5 paddle (wempe_overwind.js). Then turn the key the wrong way on a spare square held in a vice with a gauge: it must slip.
tests.pass: Nothing moves or marks: hardened, the stop bar yields at 3.63 N·m on the key and the pin at 9.87; left soft the bar bends at 1.31. The key's coil spring carries the hand: wound of spring wire Ø 0.68 or more (EN 10270-1 DH; 51 00 11 scales about 0.6, which yields at 1.57), its end in the body's hole formed on a radius. The wrong way it slips at a few mN·m (the model takes 5): one that grips both ways sends the hand into the click wheel, whose teeth yield at 0.72 N·m (the 1940 key is one-way too: its click spring, 05-01_6).

tests.title: The cannon pinion's friction
tests.when: the motion work and the hands on, the movement level
tests.how: Hang a weight on the minute hand 30 mm from its arbor, the hand horizontal, and see whether it turns the hand (the cannon pinion slipping on the centre arbor).
tests.pass: It slips between 10.3 and 443 g (wempe_motionwork.js, wempe_transmission.js's window: looser, a 45 g knock turns the hands; tighter, setting them forward drives the balance to the escapement's trip): set it near 68 g. Set the hands forward only (the 6MX's instruction: backward "can break the escape wheel's teeth"): a fit near the window's top would turn the train back against its locking stone near run-down.

tests.title: The hairspring set against the escapement
tests.sheet: 05 03_7 (the spring; no sheet gives the adjustment)
tests.when: the movement running and timed, before the trial
tests.how: Take the daily rate fully wound and again a day later without winding, or lower the swing about 10° by letting the set-up back a tooth and compare the rates over some hours each (python rating.py). A spring that loses too little on the long arcs has its terminal curves drawn in a little, or its length at the stud altered by a fraction of a turn, the adjuster's way; then vibrate the balance again (the test above).
tests.pass: With the tooth let go where 05 04_1 puts it, the impulse stone 5° inside the teeth's path, the wheel reaches the stone late after rest and this build's escapement gains 1.12 s a day for each 10° more swing (makeEsc, over the wind's 172-182°): unadjusted the rate would change 1.05 s a day over the wind. Set the spring to lose 1.12 s a day for each 10° (the spring as drawn loses less: 0.15 at 161°, 0.48 at 196°, wempe_hairspring.js): the rate then holds within 0.05 s a day over the wind. An estimate of what the adjuster did: no sheet gives it, and the drawn versions keep the drawn spring.

tests.title: The rate, and the 6MX TU's trial
tests.when: cased, in its gimbals, rated
tests.how: Each day at the same hour compare it with a time signal to a tenth of a second and log the error (python rating.py works the daily rates). The trial: 35 days in five periods of seven at 36, 20, 4, 20, 36 °C (a wine cooler, a room, a box with a lamp and a thermostat), the first two days of each not counted, wound daily after the comparison to "8" on the up-and-down dial, to "0" at each period's end.
tests.pass: The TU's figures (losing positive): E, the mean of |each counted rate − its period's mean|, within ±0.35; R = ω_V − ω_I ±2.00; D, the largest change between consecutive rates in a period, ±2.30; C = (ω36 − ω4)/32 ±0.10 s a day a °C; S = (ω36 + ω4)/2 − ω20 ±1.20; every period's mean ±3.50; N = 42E + 4.5R + 60C + 2.4S ≤ 30 (wempe_errorbudget.js passes it as adjusted). Out on C: move the four masses along the rim ("8 Körner in 60 Teilung", 6° a division) by trial: at the drawn place (30° from the cuts' line) the balance loses 2.70 s a day a °C, they null it near 18.5° from the cuts' line, a degree along the rim 0.224 s a day a °C (wempe_thermal.js). For a chronometer to navigate by (about 2 miles of longitude a month: wempe_errorbudget.js's voyage, 6 s at 30 days against 17 s with the 6MX passports' ±0.45°), go on past the TU's ±0.10: repeat the 4 °C and 36 °C periods (five counted days each, which measure C to about ±0.005) and move the masses by C / 0.224 degrees each round until |C| is within ±0.022 s a day a °C, the masses within ±0.1° of their place: 27 µm along the rim at r 15.7, both of a pair moved alike to keep the poise, against a scribed line under a 10× loupe; two or three rounds. Out on S past ±1.20: the nickel steel isn't Guillaume's integral alloy (wempe_thermal.js).

mc.note: tools/wempe_montecarlo.js: the whole Wempe made to a maker's tolerances (drawn where the sheets give them, estimated where not), judged as made and after the bench's tests (bench_wempe.json); for the Wempe's verification report

tol.note: tools/wempe_tolerances.js: how closely the Wempe's parts the drawings don't size must be made, each range keeping the swing in the guard band over the whole wind (and the sources' band, reported); read by wempe_bench.js, wempe_montecarlo.js and the Wempe's verification report

bench.note: tools/wempe_bench.js: the tests on the bench for a Wempe made to the model, each with how and what it must read, and their figures as numbers (criteria: wempe_montecarlo.js, the Wempe's verification report)

tests.title: The mainspring's torque
tests.when: before it goes into the barrel, and again in its barrel
tests.how: In its barrel, the arbor held by a lever (a 3D-printed arm 50 mm long and a hanging weight do: 1 kg at 50 mm is 0.49 N·m) or a torque gauge: wind it from slack and read the torque each half turn, then unwind and read again (the spring's friction is the difference). Leave it wound a week and read again. Once, wind it on until its coils lie tight on the arbor and count the turns from slack.
tests.pass: Set up ¾ turn past slack (05 06_20's "3/4 Umgang gespannt") and wound the drawn fusee's 5.08 barrel turns, the model's spring runs 540 to 1069 mN·m at the level 05 06_20 measures (the solved shape, wempe_physics.js); every reading within ×0.634-1.272 of it keeps the swing in the guard band over the wind and the strip under a mainspring's stress limit (wempe_tolerances.js). From slack to coil-bound it must have the set-up, the fusee's 5.08 turns and half a turn to spare (the model's 0.96 past full wind). Unwinding reads less than winding: the coils' friction gives 1-3 % on the solved spring, mainsprings 10-20 % (ICMFF9); over 22 %, clean and grease it. After the week, still in the band.

tests.title: The pull on the fusee arbor, against 05 06_20
tests.when: the chain on, the barrel set up ¾ turn, before the train goes in
tests.how: As Herb. Müller did in 1941 (05 06_20: "Hebellänge 262 m/m", the mean of two runs): a lever 262 mm long on the fusee arbor, and the weight (g) that holds it level read at each half turn running down from full wind (8.75 turns of the fusee, the curve's 0.05 to 8.74), twice; or a torque gauge (1 g on 262 mm is 2.57 mN·m).
tests.pass: Each reading within ×0.634-1.272 of the sheet's at the same turn (its readings' mean 132.7 g: 84.2-168.8 g; fully wound 138.4 g), and the run's shape the sheet's: its readings -4.7 to +4.3 % about their mean, the hump at turns 1-1.5, the dip at 4-5.75 and the rise to full wind (the solved spring through the drawn fusee fits it to 2.25 % rms). Low everywhere: the strip is thin (set up a tooth more, or a stronger strip: wempe_tolerances.js); out of shape at one end: the spring's length or set against the fusee. The sources' band, 225-270°, would want 167.9 g mean (×1.265): open (README, Unresolved).

tests.title: The train's depths
tests.when: the plates bored and reamed, before the bushes and jewels go in
tests.how: Gauge pins in each pair of holes and a micrometer, or a measuring machine, on both plates; then each mesh tried in turn with the arbors in, the escape wheel held: feel the shake at the pinion and watch the teeth through a loupe.
tests.pass: Centres 22.650, 18.120, 12.630, 11.850 mm (fusee-centre, centre-intermediate, intermediate-seconds, seconds-escape: the hole tables' coordinates), each within ±25 µm (gearing.js --model wempe: the seconds mesh's window less its pivots' shake; the tables give the places to 0.001 and no tolerance). A hole that errs should err wide: each mesh takes far more wide than close (-240/+436, -136/+355, -112/+281, -100/+263 µm). Closer than its window less the pivots' shake (220, 101, 62, 50 µm close): re-bush the hole, bored on the drawn centre.

tests.title: Endshake
tests.when: each arbor in its bearings, the plates pinned and screwed, before the escapement goes in
tests.how: Lift each arbor by its wheel with tweezers and watch its shoulder against a dial indicator, or feel it; the fusee arbor before its face a is re-turned (05 06 00-2: "bei Schneckenmontage ... Fläche a nachdrehen").
tests.pass: At 20 °C, as the Soviet Navy's 1958 MX repair book sets them (Appendix 4; the Wempe's sheets give none; the TU's 4 °C takes 3 µm of it): the centre arbor 0.07-0.10 mm (drawn 0.08, the sheets' tolerances -0.05 to 0.16), the intermediate arbor 0.07-0.10 mm (drawn 0.06, the sheets' tolerances -0.12 to 0.18), the seconds arbor 0.07-0.10 mm (drawn 0.05, the sheets' tolerances -0.14 to 0.18), the escape arbor 0.05-0.07 mm (drawn 0.06, the sheets' tolerances 0.02 to 0.08), the fusee arbor 0.08-0.12 mm (drawn 0.05, the sheets' tolerances -0.12 to 0.11), the barrel arbor 0.07-0.10 mm (drawn 0.06, the sheets' tolerances -0.13 to 0.15); the balance staff 0.04-0.06 at its endstones. The drawings' stacks come out at or just under the book's floors, so expect to free most arbors a little. The pillars' seats (0.3 +0.03 in each plate) take up to 0.06 from every arbor at once: a tight one, check the seats first. Out of the band: set the bush or jewel again, re-turn face a (the fusee), stone the shoulder.

tests.title: The balance and its hairspring vibrated
tests.when: the spring pinned to its collet and stud, its curves bent to 05 03_7, before it goes in
tests.how: Vibrate the balance on its spring in a vibrating tool (or the cock on a holder) against a master or a phone's timer: count the oscillations over two minutes, the weights against their screws' heads as drawn.
tests.pass: 2 oscillations a second (7,200 an hour), or slow by up to 367 s a day: the timing weights stand against their screws' heads as drawn and can only be screwed in, 5.0 turns of 73.4 s a day each (wempe_tolerances.js; their size estimated). The drawn spring on the weighed balance (2,501 g·mm²) is 7 min a day fast (0.4977 s): the strip wants 0.2841 mm, not 0.285 (0.2823-0.2869 over the steel's 200-210 GPa). No section tolerance holds the period (a µm of the strip is 455 s a day, the coil's ±0.05 ±173): fast, grind the strip thinner or choose a weaker spring; slow past the weights' reach, a stronger one.

tests.title: The balance runs down free
tests.when: the balance, hairspring and detent in, the train held still at a lock; before the mainspring is chosen
tests.how: Give the balance a full swing (a twist of the movement) and let it run down, the train held. Film it from above at 30 frames a second, a card marked every 30° under it, and read the swing every few seconds (python wempe_swing.py reads a video so); time how long it takes to halve from about 207°.
tests.pass: The model's balance halves its swing in 57 s (its TF 111 s, set from an earlier fit of a running 6MX on video, moMvyx8eXfo, which now gives TF 105-129 s at it: wempe_startup.js). Halving in 44, 52, 57, 62, 73, 84 s (TF 80, 100, 111, 125, 160, 200): 05 06_20's drive swings it 177, 194, 203, 213, 235, 256° at 12 h; the guard's 150° at the wind's lowest wants ×0.793, 0.680, 0.634, 0.589, 0.505, 0.448 of it, the sources' 225° ×1.620, 1.367, 1.265, 1.161, 0.980, 0.846 (the strip as the drive's cube root). Shorter than 44 s, look for a pivot, the endstone or the detent's springs dragging.

tests.title: The detent rings
tests.when: the detent made with its gold spring on, before it goes in
tests.how: Clamp its foot as the block holds it (a printed jig with the foot's screw and two steady pins), the stone and the horn free, and flick the blade's end lightly with a hair. Record the ring with a phone a few millimetres off and read its lowest strong pitch with a spectrum app, or python benchcheck.py --ring FILE.
tests.pass: 94 Hz with the spring as drawn (1436's 0.09 at its ends and "0,07" at its middle, as stiff as 0.0792 mm throughout); 68-123 Hz for a spring 0.063-0.100 mm thick, half to twice the drawn stiffness, over which the detent is home before the next tooth (dynamics.js --model wempe). The pitch goes nearly as the thickness to the 1.5 (0.050 mm 49 Hz, 0.060 mm 64 Hz, 0.063 mm 68 Hz, 0.070 mm 79 Hz, 0.079 mm 94 Hz, 0.090 mm 110 Hz, 0.100 mm 123 Hz, 0.110 mm 135 Hz: wempe_tripping.js's frame clamped at the foot), so it measures the spring's section, which no figure on 1436 settles (its "0,09" would ring 110 Hz). The gold spring rings near 2282 Hz: the detent's own is the lower.

tests.title: The escapement's figures and the banking
tests.when: the detent, its gold spring and the balance in; the train's power let down
tests.how: Turn the balance slowly by hand with a protractor card under it and read each angle through a loupe; the depth of lock and the roller's shake with feeler gauges or under a measuring microscope. The preload: wire riders of known weight hung on the stone's pipe, the detent on its banking (as the Hamilton manual's Op. 78 hangs its 0.770 g).
tests.pass: 05 04_1's layout and the model: the impulse stone's face 28°10' before the line of centres at rest, the locking stone 37.0° on in the wheel's turn and 7.14 from its centre; the gold spring met at -0.1° of the balance, the wheel released at 12.8° with the impulse stone 6.4° inside the teeth's path (05 04_1's 5°; lock 12.9°), the gold spring off the stone at 15.5° (let-off 2.7°), the return swing past it at -13.9° (overall 29.4°); roller shake 0.011 mm, the teeth 0.39 mm into the roller. Set the banking (the block's cross screw, the 1954 instruction's п. 11) for a lock 0.188 mm deep at the stone, the middle of its window (the drawing's 0.235 lies 134 µm over its floor): never shallower than 0.101 (a held tooth's stone rings more than half the depth: wempe_build.js's frame) nor deeper than 0.275 (the discharge stone can't lift the stone further: it doesn't unlock). A wheel at the top of its 14 +0.03 locks 0.250 deep where the drawn wheel locks 0.235: set the banking to the wheel as made. The return pass: turn the balance back slowly by hand through the discharge with the train's power on and watch the locking stone under a loupe: the discharge stone must bend the gold spring aside without lifting the detent (wempe_tripping.js: as the model takes the stone's contact on the gold spring no tooth gets past over 333 gold's whole range of modulus, 83-110 GPa, but at 4 times that contact's stiffness 6 in 12 do, whatever the alloy: only the made spring can show it); its tip at rest 0.10-0.15 short of the discharge stone and 0.35-0.40 past the detent's end (the 1958 Navy repair book's checks, p. 60).

tests.title: The swing
tests.when: the movement running, fully wound, at 24 h and near run-down
tests.how: Read the balance's swing against marks under it, from a phone's slow-motion video (python wempe_swing.py reads the arm's sweep), or from a recording of the beat (python acoustic.py --model wempe FILE fits its clicks to the escapement in time).
tests.pass: In the guard band, 150-270° each way, over the whole wind (the model 196.8-209.4°, 203.1° at 12 h). The sources' band, 225-270° (the 1954 instruction, chronometers in general; the Hamilton manual 247.5-270°), is reported, not required: the model's swing is under it on 05 06_20's drive (open, README). Low at both ends with the train free: the strip doesn't suit the balance's damping (the run-down test chooses it), or the preload is high; low at one end only: the fusee's test.

windows.note: tools/gearing.js --model wempe: the Wempe's meshes, each one's depthing window about its drawn centres (mm), the hole position tolerance (mm) aimed at them, its pivots' shake (sh, mm), its mean pressure angle (deg, frictionless contact) and its mean torque ratio against the nominal at mu 0, 0.10, 0.20 (eff: the mesh's efficiency); read by wempe_physics.js

json.sure: the alias (A + 90 k) certain in every window (the next 1.4-2.1 lower against scores of 3.1-3.6, the frames between the turning points deciding); each reading to about 2 deg against its neighbours; the scale (the ellipse's affine angle at a 0.90 view, the staff's image fitted per stretch) a few percent, and between stretches the staff and ellipse are fitted anew (3 % between them moves wempe_startup.js's TF 13 %)
